newsitem.title: MEXICO: DNA Plant Tech shareholders approve merger. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: DNA Plant Tech shareholders approve merger. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: Shareholders of DNA Plant Technology Corp have approved a proposed merger with a unit of Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna SA, according to company officials at La Moderna.
"The merger has been approved," Alfonso (corrects from Pablo) Romo, CEO of Grupo Pulsar, the controlling group of La Moderna, told Reuters.
La Moderna will fuse the Oakland-based DNA Plant Technology with its Bionova produce unit and create a new company, DNAP Holding Corp.

Each ordinary share of DNA Plant Technology will be converted to 0.1 ordinary shares of DNAP Holding and each preferred share of DNA Plant Technology will become 0.68375 ordinary shares of DNAP Holding, La Moderna said in a news release.
La Moderna will hold a 70 percent stake in the new company, whose shares will be listed in the Nasdaq market as.

La Moderna, a conglomerate with interests in cigarettes, packaging and fast-growing fresh-vegetables and vegetable-seed divisions, announced earlier this week that it had reached an agreement to sell its non-vegetable seed division to the St. Louis-based Monsanto Co.
La Moderna plans to use biotechnology created at DNAP Holding to help both its Bionova fresh-produce business and the vegetable-seed-producing unit Seminis.

"According to our objectives, DNAP Holding will have a leading role in the development and commercialization of high-quality fresh produce at a world level," Romo was quoted as saying in the news release.

"Furthermore, in combining our produce business with the scientific strength of DNAP we take another important step in achieving our objective of being world leaders in the agrobiotechnology and seed industries, which complements and strengthens our recent technology-sharing agreement with Monsanto."
As part of the merger, La Moderna signed an agreement to create a research and development fund worth $30 million at DNAP over the course of the next 10 years.
La Moderna also agreed to allow at least four indepenedent members on the board of directors of DNAP Holding.
